papers.title: Temperature-Dependent Rheological and Viscoelastic Investigation of a Poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline)-b-poly(2-
papers.abstract: The synthesis and characterization of an ABA triblock copolymer based on hydrophilic poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline) (pMeOx) blocks A and a modestly hydrophobic poly(2-iso-butyl-2-oxazoline) (piBuOx) block B is described. Aqueous polymer solutions were prepared at different concentrations (1-20 wt %) and their thermogelling capability using visual observation was investigated at different temperatures ranging from 5 to 80 °C. As only a 20 wt % solution was found to undergo thermogelation, this concentration was investigated in more detail regarding its temperature-dependent viscoelastic profile utilizing various modes (strain or temperature sweep). The prepared hydrogels from this particular ABA triblock copolymer have interesting rheological and viscoelastic properties, such as reversible thermogelling and shear thinning, and may be used as bioink, which was supported by its very low cytotoxicity and initial printing experiments using the hydrogels. However, the soft character and low yield stress of the gels do not allow real 3D printing at this point.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究了温敏性三嵌段共聚物的流变学特性及作为生物墨水的可能性，但未涉及任何人工智能方法。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate AI into any bioprinting workflow stage; it only provides basic material characterization and preliminary printing tests without intelligent control or optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种具有温敏性和剪切变稀特性的可逆凝胶生物墨水。
summary_zh.method: 合成pMeOx-piBuOx-pMeOx三嵌段共聚物，通过流变学测试表征其凝胶行为。
summary_zh.result: 20 wt%溶液发生热凝胶化，凝胶具有剪切变稀和低细胞毒性，但机械强度不足以实现3D打印。
summary_zh.validation: 通过流变测试、细胞毒性实验和初步打印实验验证材料性能。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a thermoreversible hydrogel bioink with shear-thinning properties for bioprinting applications.
summary_en.method: An ABA triblock copolymer of poly(2-methyl-2-oxazoline) and poly(2-iso-butyl-2-oxazoline) was synthesized, and its aqueous solutions were characterized by rheological measurements.
summary_en.result: Only a 20 wt% solution exhibited thermogelation, showing reversible gelation and shear thinning, but the gel's softness and low yield stress prevented successful 3D printing.
summary_en.validation: Validation included rheological analysis, cytotoxicity assays, and preliminary printing tests.
